keywords: Geoinformatics 2.Photogrammetry and Laser Surveying 3.GNSS, Remote Sensing, and GIS 4.Spatial Information Processing 5.Spatial Information Literacy
educationalGoal: Based on the KIT-IDEALS code of conduct, the learning objectives aim to cultivate engineers capable of achieving the educational goals of the Department of Environmental and Civil Engineering. Students will acquire the ability to plan, implement, and evaluate solutions to challenges through the utilization of spatial information, and learn to manage their own project processes. Through these activities, students will complete reports for Project Design III from an academic perspective, comparable to research papers or reports.
advice: At the Geoinformatics Laboratory(Nakano Lab.), projects center on surveying and geomatics. Students select topics from faculty proposals, spatial information projects, or self‑devised themes, with advanced tracks for those moving on to graduate study. Work is student‑led: think independently, act proactively, report to faculty, share with the lab, and refine with guidance. Students learn process and schedule management, practice self‑management, and execute planned research. Participation in the KIT Spatial Information Project and related events deepens understanding of advanced applications. In the first semester, students iterate literature summaries, presentations, and Q&A, while building spatial information literacy through hands‑on use of core tools (GIS, GNSS, remote sensing/photogrammetry, LiDAR). They deepen investigation of their themes and periodically consolidate findings, revising scope as needed. In the second semester, they conduct hypothesis testing, empirical experiments, analysis, and interpretation, individually or in teams, to raise project completeness. Weekly meetings provide progress reporting, with monthly reviews, plus active participation in KIT seminars. Total learning time is about 450 hours, including summer and winter activities; preparation and review time in the learning support plan is a minimum requirement.
books: Textbooks:None Reference books:Spatial Information Technology [Japan Survey Association] Reserved books:None
requiredKnowledge: Students should review previously studied materials such as Surveying I and II, Surveying Practicum/Exercise I and II, spatial information technology, Environmental Civil Engineering Experiments/Exercise III. They should review the textbooks and materials used in this course.

achievementLevels.ideal: Students will acquire fundamental knowledge in geoinformatics and be able to clearly and comprehensively explain its application fields across various technologies. This includes knowledge and application areas of the technologies underpinning geoinformatics: satellite positioning systems (GNSS), remote sensing (RS), geographic information systems (GIS), photogrammetry, and laser surveying. Students will be able to appropriately select and operate software related to each technology, perform advanced analysis, and develop programs as needed.
achievementLevels.standard: Students will acquire and be able to outline fundamental knowledge of geoinformatics. This includes knowledge of and application fields for technologies supporting geoinformatics, such as satellite positioning systems (GNSS), remote sensing (RS), geographic information systems (GIS), photogrammetry, and laser surveying. Students will be able to operate designated software for each technology and generate analysis results using standard functions.
